author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Making Your Own PCSX2 HD Texture Packs on Steam OS / Linux
summary: T Man develops a PCSX2 texture-pack workflow on SteamOS and Linux, documenting dumping rules, sorting, AI-upscale failures and Steam Deck constraints instead of presenting replacement art as a one-click enhancement.

blocks.text: The unusually detailed notes explain why texture creation is iterative. Assets already present in the replacements directory do not redump, and existing dumps remain suppressed until dumping is toggled or the game resets; that behavior can prevent duplicate work but can also confuse a creator who expects every frame to produce files. The guide preserves original dumps because automated upscaling succeeds unevenly, and it calls out Budokai 3 interface and map elements that resist a clean pipeline. Linux tooling and SteamOS package constraints are addressed directly.

The published Deck tuning reflects one undervolted LCD unit and an April 2024-era software stack, so its SMT, clock and GPU advice should not be copied to other revisions without measurement. AI-processed textures can invent detail, break alpha, alter typography or exceed memory budgets; creators must review every asset and respect the source artwork’s rights. Keep untouched dumps, version the replacement set, record the game serial, and test transitions as well as menus. The tutorial is a production diary, not a universal performance preset.
